what: Build Check Part 2 (wording check), statements version 0.3, 7 October 2026. Only the statements that changed since the version before were checked again.

statements_checked.question: Which months do I prune my rose?
statements_checked.text: In most areas, the main winter pruning is done in July. In some places it can start in June. Months are only a guide, because frosts vary from year to year.

statements_checked.question: Which months do I prune my rose?
statements_checked.text: In a cold or frosty area, wait until August to prune, so that frost does not damage the new shoots. Months are only a guide, because frosts vary from year to year.

statements_checked.question: Which months do I prune my rose?
statements_checked.text: In New South Wales, one rose society says to prune in July near the coast, where frosts are rare or never come, and that you can start in late June. Inland, or where frosts are regular, it says to prune in August. Months are only a guide, because frosts vary from year to year.
statements_checked.shown_to: Gardeners in New South Wales only

statements_checked.question: Which months do I prune my rose?
statements_checked.text: In Victoria, one rose society says the best time to prune is June or July. In a cold area, it says to wait until August, so that frost does not knock back the new shoots. Months are only a guide, because frosts vary from year to year.

statements_checked.question: Which months do I prune my rose?
statements_checked.text: In South Australia, prune in July. One nursery says pruning can start in late June. Months are only a guide, because frosts vary from year to year.

statements_checked.question: Which months do I prune my rose?
statements_checked.text: For a frost area in South Australia, one rose society says to wait until August to prune, and one nursery says July. Months are only a guide, because frosts vary from year to year.

statements_checked.question: Which months do I prune my rose?
statements_checked.text: In Western Australia, one rose society says to prune in winter, in June and July. Months are only a guide.

statements_checked.question: Which months do I prune my rose?
statements_checked.text: In Brisbane, one public rose garden says the best time to prune is June or July. Months are only a guide.
statements_checked.shown_to: Gardeners in or near Brisbane only

statements_checked.question: Which months do I prune my rose?
statements_checked.text: I couldn't find months for rose jobs written for Tasmania. A local rose society is the place to ask.

statements_checked.question: Which months do I prune my rose?
statements_checked.text: I couldn't find months for rose jobs written for the Northern Territory. A local garden society or botanic garden is the place to ask.
statements_checked.shown_to: Gardeners in the Northern Territory only

statements_checked.question: Which months do I prune my rose?
statements_checked.text: I couldn't find months for rose jobs written for Queensland, apart from pruning in Brisbane. A local rose society is the place to ask.

statements_checked.question: Which months do I prune my rose?
statements_checked.text: I couldn't find months for rose jobs written for the dry inland of Australia, such as Mildura. A local rose society is the place to ask.
statements_checked.shown_to: Gardeners in New South Wales or in Victoria or in Queensland or in South Australia or in Western Australia only

statements_checked.question: When do I start and stop feeding?
statements_checked.text: Start feeding after the winter prune, as new growth appears. One nursery waits until the rose has plenty of leaves and its first blooms.

statements_checked.question: When do I start and stop feeding?
statements_checked.text: Give the spring feed in the second half of August or in September. Months are only a guide.

statements_checked.question: When do I start and stop feeding?
statements_checked.text: Give the last feed in late summer or early autumn, in February or March. One nursery says not to feed in late autumn. Months are only a guide.

statements_checked.question: When do I start and stop feeding?
statements_checked.text: In New South Wales, one rose society says to give the first feed after the winter prune, ideally in the second half of August, or in September in a cold area. It says to give the last feed in mid to late February. Months are only a guide.
statements_checked.shown_to: Gardeners in New South Wales only

statements_checked.question: When do I start and stop feeding?
statements_checked.text: In Victoria, one rose society says to feed roses at the end of August. For a newly planted bare-root rose (a dormant plant sold in winter, with no leaves or flowers), it says to wait until late November or early December, and then to feed at half the recommended amount. Months are only a guide.

statements_checked.question: When do I start and stop feeding?
statements_checked.text: In South Australia, feed in September and again in February. One rose society says early in September, and in March if you missed February. On sandy soil, it says to feed four times: in September, November, February and April. Months are only a guide.

statements_checked.question: When do I start and stop feeding?
statements_checked.text: In Western Australia, one rose society says to feed as new growth appears in early spring, in August or September, and to keep feeding into May. Months are only a guide.

statements_checked.question: When do I stop deadheading?
statements_checked.text: I couldn't find a month to stop deadheading (cutting off the finished blooms) in Australia. A local rose society is the place to ask.

statements_checked.question: When do I stop deadheading?
statements_checked.text: To bring on flowers in autumn, give the rose a light trim in summer or early autumn. This is done between January and March, depending on where you live. Months are only a guide.

statements_checked.question: When do I stop deadheading?
statements_checked.text: In New South Wales, one rose society says to trim roses for flowers in autumn: in January in a cool area, early in February in a mild area, and in March in a warm area. Months are only a guide.
statements_checked.shown_to: Gardeners in New South Wales only

statements_checked.question: When do I stop deadheading?
statements_checked.text: In Victoria, one rose society says to give a summer trim in February if you are timing the flowers for a show or special event. It also says to deadhead in April. Months are only a guide.

statements_checked.question: When do I stop deadheading?
statements_checked.text: In South Australia, a light trim in late summer or early autumn brings on the autumn flowers. One nursery says mid February, and one rose society says one to two weeks after the February feed. Months are only a guide.

statements_checked.question: When do I stop deadheading?
statements_checked.text: In Western Australia, one rose society says to give a light prune, taking off about one-third, in March or April, and to keep deadheading into May. Months are only a guide.

statements_checked.question: Which months do I plant or move a rose?
statements_checked.text: In Australia, plant a bare-root rose (a dormant plant sold in winter, with no leaves or flowers) in June or July. One source says planting can start in May. Months are only a guide.

statements_checked.question: Which months do I plant or move a rose?
statements_checked.text: Move an established rose in winter, while it is dormant.

statements_checked.question: Which months do I plant or move a rose?
statements_checked.text: Don't plant a rose in very hot weather.

statements_checked.question: Which months do I plant or move a rose?
statements_checked.text: In New South Wales, one rose society says to prepare the soil in late April or May, for planting in June or July. Months are only a guide.
statements_checked.shown_to: Gardeners in New South Wales only

statements_checked.question: Which months do I plant or move a rose?
statements_checked.text: In Sydney, one garden centre says a rose in a pot can be planted at any time of year, though not in very hot weather.
statements_checked.shown_to: Gardeners in or near Sydney only

statements_checked.question: Which months do I plant or move a rose?
statements_checked.text: In Victoria, one rose society says to order new roses in May and start planting them in June. It also says to move an established rose in June. Months are only a guide.

statements_checked.question: Which months do I plant or move a rose?
statements_checked.text: In South Australia, plant a bare-root rose in June or July. Planting can go on into August. Months are only a guide.

statements_checked.question: Which months do I plant or move a rose?
statements_checked.text: In Western Australia, one rose society says to plant new roses in May, and to plant or repot as needed in June and July. Months are only a guide.

statements_checked.question: When do I clear up and spray in winter?
statements_checked.text: After the winter prune, pick off any leaves left on the rose, clear up the prunings and fallen leaves, and get rid of them. One source says to put them in the rubbish bin, not the compost.

statements_checked.question: When do I clear up and spray in winter?
statements_checked.text: If you use a clean-up spray in winter (a spray to clear pests and diseases left on the plant), put it on after pruning. Lime sulphur and a spraying oil are two of the types used. Follow the label on the spray.

statements_checked.question: When do I clear up and spray in winter?
statements_checked.text: If you use lime sulphur as a winter spray, put it on while the rose is dormant, before new growth appears. One source says lime sulphur burns new growth. Follow the label on the spray.

statements_checked.question: When do I clear up and spray in winter?
statements_checked.text: In New South Wales, one rose society says to put the prunings and fallen leaves in the green waste bin as soon as pruning is finished, and then to spray. It says lime sulphur is effective. Follow the label on the spray.
statements_checked.shown_to: Gardeners in New South Wales only

statements_checked.question: When do I clear up and spray in winter?
statements_checked.text: In Victoria, one rose society says to take all the leaves off the bushes and rake up around the beds in July, and then to spray the bare roses and, lightly, the ground around them. Follow the label on the spray. Months are only a guide.

statements_checked.question: When do I clear up and spray in winter?
statements_checked.text: In South Australia, clear up the prunings and fallen leaves after pruning, in July or August, and then spray. Lime sulphur, copper and a spraying oil are the sprays used. Follow the label on the spray. Months are only a guide.

statements_checked.question: When do I clear up and spray in winter?
statements_checked.text: In Western Australia, one rose society says to spray after pruning, in June or July, to clean up pests and disease. Follow the label on the spray. Months are only a guide.

statements_checked.question: When do I clear up and spray in winter?
statements_checked.text: I couldn't find Australian advice on covering roses or mounding soil over the base for winter. A local rose society is the place to ask.

statements_checked.question: How do I allow for frost and my own garden?
statements_checked.text: In an area that gets frosts, wait until the last frost has passed before you prune.

statements_checked.question: How do I allow for frost and my own garden?
statements_checked.text: Large areas of northern Australia are generally free of frost, the national weather bureau says. Days cold enough for frost fall mainly between late autumn and early spring.

statements_checked.question: How do I allow for frost and my own garden?
statements_checked.text: Frost is local: how severe it is can vary a lot over a very small area, the national weather bureau says. Frost can form in a valley while the land around it stays free of it.

statements_checked.question: How do I allow for frost and my own garden?
statements_checked.text: In a humid climate, roses are more likely to get fungal diseases, and one source says roses are harder to manage in the hot tropics. Another says to choose a rose that is not prone to these diseases if your climate is humid.

statements_checked.question: How do I allow for frost and my own garden?
statements_checked.text: In South Australia, one rose society says frosts are common in country areas, and that it is colder and wetter in the Adelaide Hills, the South-East, and Southern Yorke Peninsula and Eyre Peninsula.

results.note: Supported, Moderate. July: SARS-CAL, SARS-WIN and RSSA-GG (one society) and ROSS-CAL 'Pruning time in most districts'. Late June: ROSS-CAL alone, said as one nursery. The frost sentence has moved to item 6, so the label now covers only what two voices agree on.

Supported and rightly marked 'Sources disagree' with no level (rules section 3A). RSSA-GG: 'Pruning is best done in July (or August in frost areas).' ROSS-CAL, under July: 'In frosty districts delay pruning until now.' One society against one nursery, each side said, neither led with beyond the order. It stands alone, names the place and the condition in words, and says months are only a guide. It sits beside the national 'wait until August' (item 2) without contradicting it.

A gap, marked as one, true for every Queensland gardener including Brisbane: the only Queensland months found are NFP's June or July for pruning in Brisbane. AF-71 now says the same. Points to local help.

Supported, one organisation, said so, Low. RSNSW-CAL: 'Immediately pruning is completed, the prunings and fallen leaves should be put in the green waste bin and the plants sprayed with a fungicide'; 'Lime Sulphur is recognised as being effective'. 'And then to spray' says less than the page, which is allowed, and the unexplained word is gone. No month is named, so no month line is needed.

package_notes: Nothing is still wrong or newly wrong in these four. Version 0.3 (46 statements) passes the structural checks: traces exist, labels match the first finding's level, the disagreement statement carries no level, every available finding is used, and every statement that names a month says months are only a guide.
